metadata.title: Bullion Sales Tax in West Virginia (2026): Rules & Exemptions

description: West Virginia has a statewide sales tax, but qualifying gold/silver bullion and certain coins are fully exempt. Jewelry is taxable; nonqualifying items are taxed.

What's covered by the exemption
Qualifying gold/silver bullion and certain coins
How they decide what counts as bullion
The state asks whether the item is priced for its metal value (qualifying bullion) or for rarity, design, or collector demand (taxable).
What's NOT covered
Jewelry, rarity-priced collectibles, paper currency held as collectible, fabricated/industrial-use precious metal, and accessories.
Common questions about sales tax on gold and silver in West Virginia.
Is gold bullion sales-tax exempt in West Virginia?
+
Yes. Qualifying gold bullion is fully exempt from West Virginia sales tax under the statewide rule.
Is silver bullion sales-tax exempt in West Virginia?
+
Yes. Qualifying silver bullion is fully exempt, as long as it meets the state’s investment bullion/coin criteria.
Are coins exempt from sales tax in West Virginia?
+
Certain coins are exempt when they qualify under West Virginia’s bullion/coin criteria; nonqualifying coins can be taxable.
Do I pay sales tax on numismatic coins in West Virginia?
+
Sometimes. Numismatic items are conditional and may be taxed if they do not qualify as exempt bullion or qualifying coins.
Is precious-metal jewelry taxed in West Virginia?
+
Yes. Jewelry is taxable in West Virginia even though qualifying bullion and certain coins are exempt.
